title: Classic Trance — Trance Archetype #9 (vi-V-IV-III)
theory_notes: [Obsidian: 9 Trance Chord Progressions For Powerful & Exhilarating Tracks] The vi-V-IV-III progression brings a unique twist to trance music, offering a blend of melancholy and resolution that can be deeply moving. This is evident in Andrew Rayel’s “My Reflection” (which was originally posted with a different progression), where the progression adds a profound emotional depth to the track. Starting with the relative minor (vi) sets an introspective tone, followed by the dominant (V) which introduces a sense of urgency. Then, it moves to the subdominant (IV) for a moment of calm, and finally, the mediant (III) offers an unexpected but satisfying resolution.

title: Euphoric Trance — The euphoric minor loop
theory_notes: [Obsidian: Trance Chord Progressions: 6 Euphoric Loops + Free MIDI] If you only learn one trance progression, make it this one. It starts sad on Am, then rises through three major chords and never fully settles, so it keeps pulling you into the next bar. One chord per bar, looped for the whole breakdown and drop. Voicing tip: keep your right hand in one spot. Am as A, C, E, then F as A, C, F, then C as G, C, E and G as G, B, D. Only one or two notes move each time, which keeps a wide supersaw from turning into mush.
